questions.question: Two statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they do not conform to real-world knowledge, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows from the statements. Statements: All ponds are pools. Some wells are ponds.

Conclusions:

I. Some ponds are not wells.

II. Some wells are pools.

III. All pools are wells.
questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is as follows:

I. Some ponds are not wells → False (It is possible but not definite)

Hence, only conclusion II follows.

(6, 9, 18)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number × 1.5 = 2nd number)

(2nd number × 2 = 3rd number)

Now,

(6 × 1.5 = 9)

(9 × 2 = 18)

Similarly, for (14, 21, 42)

(14 × 1.5 = 21)

(21 × 2 = 42).

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

(n, n × 1.5, n × 3)

2) (8, 14, 24) → does not follow the rule as 8 × 1.5 = 12 ≠ 14

3) (14, 21, 42) → (14, 14 × 1.5 = 21, 14 × 3 = 42) and hence, follows the rule

questions.question: In ΔABC, D is a point on AC such that AB = BD = DC, if ∠BAD = 70°, then the measure of ∠B is:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, D is a point on AC such that AB = BD = DC, if ∠BAD = 70°, then the measure of ∠B is:
questions.solution:
Given, AB = BD = DC

And ∠BAD = 70°

In ΔABD,

⇒ ∠BAD = ∠BDA = 70° [∵ AB = BD]

⇒ ∠ABD + ∠BAD + ∠BDA = 180°

⇒ ∠ABD = 180° – 70° – 70° = 40°

⇒ ∠BDC = 180° – ∠BDA = 180° – 70° = 110°

In ΔBDC,

⇒ ∠DBC = ∠DCB [∵ BD = DC]

⇒ ∠DBC + ∠BDC + ∠DCB = 180°

⇒ 2∠DBC = 180° – 110° = 70°

⇒ ∠DBC = 35°

⇒ ∠ABC = ∠ABD + ∠DBC = 40° + 35° = 75°

questions.questionHtml: A train travelling at 44 km/h crosses a man walking with a speed of 8 km/h, in the same direction, in 15 seconds. If the train crosses a woman coming from the opposite direction in 10 seconds, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the woman?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative Speed (Same direction) = 44 − 8 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s.

Length of Train = 10 × 15 = 150 m.

Relative Speed (Opposite direction) = 150 ÷ 10 = 15 m/s = 54 km/h.

Woman Speed = 54 − 44 = 10 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given: Speed of Train (ST) = 44 km/h, Speed of Man (SM) = 8 km/h, Time to cross man (t1) = 15 s, Time to cross Woman (t2) = 10 s.

Formula Used: Distance = Relative Speed × Time; 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s.

⇒ Relative speed with man = 44 − 8 = 36 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/s = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s

⇒ Length of train (L) = Speed × Time = 10 × 15 = 150 m

⇒ Let the speed of woman be x km/h. Relative speed (opposite) = (44 + x) km/h

⇒ Length = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 150 = (44 + x) × (5/18) × 10

⇒ 15 = (44 + x) × 5/18

⇒ 270 = 220 + 5x → No, simpler: 15 × 18 / 5 = 44 + x

⇒ 54 = 44 + x

⇒ x = 10 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is S1 − S2. In the opposite direction, it is S1 + S2.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Moving Object

The distance covered while crossing a person is equal to the length of the train itself, regardless of the person's speed.

questions.question: If a + b + c = 2, a 2 + b 2 + c 2 = 26, then the value of a 3 + b 3 + c 3 – 3abc is:
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c = 2, a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> = 26, then the value of a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3</sup> – 3abc is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For expressions of the form a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc, use the direct formula:

Value = (a + b + c) ÷ 2 × [3(a2 + b2 + c2) − (a + b + c)2]

⇒ Value = (2 ÷ 2) × [3(26) − (2)2]

⇒ Value = 1 × [78 − 4] = 74

∴ The correct answer is 74.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sum of terms: a + b + c = 2

Sum of squares: a2 + b2 + c2 = 26

Formula Used:

1. (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

2. a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − (ab + bc + ca))

Calculations:

First, find the value of (ab + bc + ca):

⇒ (2)2 = 26 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 4 = 26 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = 4 − 26

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = −22

⇒ ab + bc + ca = −11

Now, substitute the values into the cubic identity:

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 2 × [26 − (−11)]

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 2 × [26 + 11]

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 2 × 37

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 74

∴ The correct answer is 74.

Additional Information

Special Case (a + b + c = 0)

If the sum of the three variables is zero, then a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

Alternative Form of Cubic Identity

a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c) × [(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2].

Condition for Zero Result

The expression a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc equals zero if either a + b + c = 0 or a = b = c.

questions.question: In ΔACE, B and D are the points on side AC and CE, respectively, such that BD || AE and AE/BD = 8/3. What is the ratio of the area of ΔBDC to that of ΔAEC?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔACE, B and D are the points on side AC and CE, respectively, such that BD || AE and AE/BD = 8/3. What is the ratio of the area of ΔBDC to that of ΔAEC?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Given BD || AE, ΔBDC is similar to ΔAEC (ΔBDC ~ ΔAEC).

Ratio of sides BD : AE = 3 : 8.

⇒ Ratio of Area(ΔBDC) : Area(ΔAEC) = (3)2 : (8)2 = 9 : 64.

∴ The correct answer is 9 : 64.

Alternate Method

Given:

In ΔACE, BD || AE and AE/BD = 8/3.

Formula Used:

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Calculations:

In ΔBDC and ΔAEC:

⇒ ∠C = ∠C (Common angle)

⇒ ∠CBD = ∠CAE (Corresponding angles as BD || AE)

⇒ ∠CDB = ∠CEA (Corresponding angles as BD || AE)

⇒ ∴ ΔBDC ~ ΔAEC (By AAA similarity criterion)

⇒ Area(ΔBDC) / Area(ΔAEC) = (BD / AE)2

⇒ Given AE/BD = 8/3 → BD/AE = 3/8

⇒ Area(ΔBDC) / Area(ΔAEC) = (3 / 8)2

⇒ Area(ΔBDC) / Area(ΔAEC) = 9 / 64

∴ The correct answer is 9 : 64.

Additional Information

Similar Triangles Properties

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their altitudes, medians, and perimeters is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Thales Theorem (BPT)

A line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio (CB/BA = CD/DE).

Area Ratio Rule

For any two similar figures, the ratio of their areas is always the square of the ratio of any linear dimension (side, radius, etc.).

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. It is one of the highly developed countries of the world. B. So, the correct order is DBCA.

B. The Norwegian Government decided to evacuate the passengers with the help of helicopters.
